_comment: Copy this to <your repo>/video/narration.json, then replace every <PLACEHOLDER>. generate-narration.py refuses to synthesize while any < or > remains. Keys starting with an underscore are ignored by the pipeline.
_comment_provider: elevenlabs reads the key from ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, then XI_API_KEY, then ELEVEN_LABS_KEY. google uses the gcloud access token of whoever is logged in, and reads languageCode, voice and speakingRate instead.
_comment_beats: Seven beats, one per thing a judge has to be told. captionText is what the viewer reads. speechText is what the voice says. They are separate fields on purpose: captions carry the exact product names, spellings and figures a judge will check, and speech carries the spelled-out form a TTS engine pronounces correctly. So DataHub in a caption is Data Hub in speech, MCP is M C P, PR 183 is pull request one eighty three. Contract: each field 20 to 800 characters, ids matching [a-z][a-z-]{1,24}, each beat 3 to 40 seconds of measured speech, whole video 90 to 174 seconds. The real length of this template with a real voice has NOT been measured, so do not plan around a number for it: run the generator once and read the total it prints. It fails outside the 90 to 174 second window and tells you the measured figure, so cut or add words after that first run rather than guessing. Record the browser capture only after you know the total, because the capture must be at least trimLeadSeconds plus that total or the build will reject it.
